transcript.text: Every so often when I use the hob the electrics in the house go off. Not every time, maybe once a week. It's an induction hob, Hisense I think.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. An induction hob tripping your house electrics is almost always an earth leakage fault—meaning electricity is escaping where it shouldn't and triggering your RCD (the safety switch that cuts power to prevent shock). It can also be a simple overload if the hob draws more current than the circuit is rated for, but given it's intermittent, leakage is the primary suspect. Because this involves mains voltage and potential earth faults, please do not attempt to open the hob or test internal components yourself. If you smell burning plastic or see scorch marks, stop using it immediately and isolate it at the fused spur/consumer unit. To help me guide you on what an engineer will likely need to check (or if there's a simple setting issue), could you tell me:
1. Does the trip happen instantly when you switch a zone on, or only after some time?
2. Is it always one specific cooking zone that causes it, or does any zone trigger it?

Not sure if it's instant or after a while, I've not really noticed. It's usually when I've got two rings on high, and a couple of times it was when something boiled over. I don't know if it's one particular ring. Once there was a faint electrical smell after it tripped too.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. The faint electrical smell combined with the tripping is a clear safety warning. This indicates an earth leakage fault—electricity is escaping from the high-voltage induction components (the coils or power modules) to the metal casing or wiring. Because this involves mains voltage and potential fire risk, you must not use the hob again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has inspected it. They will need to check for earth faults in the power modules and the wiring at the fused spur. Please leave the hob isolated (switched off at the consumer unit) and arrange for a professional inspection.

candidates: Earth leakage fault (induction coil or power module) (high)
Overloaded circuit / MCB tripping due to high current draw (medium)
